messages.content: Roblox or Fortnite UEFN for my next kids' tower-defense game?

For you, **Roblox first**.

- **Audience:** Roblox 123M DAU (Q2 2026), 35% of age-checked users under 13 [P]. Fortnite has 75M+ MAU and skews older [S].
- **Payouts:** Roblox paid $1.50B DevEx in 2025 [P]. Fortnite has paid $1B+ to UEFN creators since 2023 [S].
- **Eligibility:** Fortnite engagement payouts need you to be **18+** [P].
- **Skills:** you already know Luau/Studio; UEFN means Unreal + Verse.

Fortnite is a good *second* platform: islands took 47% of Fortnite hours in May 2026 [S], and in-island sales pay 100% of V-Bucks value until Jan 31, 2027 (50% after) [P]. Port a proven Roblox game later rather than starting there.
How does Roblox DevEx work in money terms?

Since Sept 5, 2025, Robux you *earn* convert at **$0.0038 each** (was $0.0035) [P]. So 10,000 earned Robux = $38; 100,000 = $380.

Things that reduce what you keep:
- You earn only a share of what players spend in your game (Roblox's marketplace fee applies to sales).
- Robux earned before Sept 5, 2025 convert at the old rate.
- There are eligibility rules (minimum earned Robux, age, account standing). Historically 13+ and 30,000 Robux [U]; check the Help Center before relying on it.

For context, Roblox paid creators $1.503B through DevEx in 2025, and the top 1,000 creators averaged $1.3M [P]. Most creators earn far less.
What are Roblox Creator Rewards and how do I earn them?

Two rewards, live since July 24, 2025 [P]:

1. **Daily Engagement:** 5 Robux each day an *Active Spender* (spent ≥ $9.99 on Roblox in the last 60 days) plays your game ≥10 minutes, if it's one of the first 3 games they launch that day.
2. **Audience Expansion:** 35% of a new or returning user's first $100 of purchases anywhere on Roblox in their first 60 days, if they came via your share link, a direct link, or a search for your game's name and played 10+ minutes. Requires an ID-verified account.

Design takeaways: be a game kids open *first* each day (daily goals, friends), and give players a reason to share your link (invite rewards that don't need spending).
How do Fortnite creators get paid?

Two ways [P]:

1. **Engagement payouts:** 40% of eligible Fortnite net revenue (after platform fees) goes into a pool, split monthly across all islands, Epic's own included, by engagement from paying players. Sponsored Row revenue also adds to the pool (100% through end of 2026).
2. **In-island transactions** (since Jan 9, 2026): creators get 100% of V-Bucks value through Jan 31, 2027, then 50% from Feb 1, 2027. Items capped at 5,000 V-Bucks; random items must show odds [S].

You must be **18+** for payouts, with a $100 minimum payout threshold [P]. Epic says it has paid UEFN creators $1B+ since 2023 [S].
I'm 15. Which platform can I actually earn on?

Roblox is the realistic one.
- Fortnite engagement payouts require you to be **18+** [P].
- Minecraft Marketplace works through approved partners, usually companies or teams [U].
- Roblox has historically allowed DevEx from age 13 with enough earned Robux and good standing [U]. Check the current Help Center rules and involve a parent/guardian for payments and tax.

Start on Roblox, keep your game kid-safe, and save the Fortnite idea for later.
Is there any risk in building only on one platform?

Yes. Platform risk is real:
- **Rec Room shut down on June 1, 2026**, after failing to become profitable [S]. Creators' worlds there are gone.
- Roblox changed age checks, disabled cross-experience game-pass sales, and moved recommendations to a 28-day retention window in 2026; bookings guidance turned negative [P].
- Fortnite's in-island revenue share drops from 100% to 50% in Feb 2027 [P].

Reduce it: keep design docs, art source files and code clean and portable; read every quarterly letter and DevForum announcement; build an audience channel you control (e.g. a Roblox group); and once one game works, consider a second platform.
What about Minecraft Marketplace?

Big kid brand, harder entry.
- Minecraft had **155M monthly active users** (Microsoft, Oct 2025, latest official) [P]. Tracker claims of ~212M are unverified [U].
- Marketplace sells skins, worlds, texture packs and add-ons for Minecoins on Bedrock; reported $500M+ paid to creators since 2017 [U].
- Selling requires being an approved **Marketplace Partner**, usually a company/team [U]. Revenue share reported ~70% but unconfirmed [U].
- Discovery is a curated store; there's no public CCU chart, so it's hard to research.

For a solo dev making TD games for kids, Roblox is faster to start and easier to measure. Revisit Minecraft once you have a team or portfolio.
What about Zepeto, s&box or Steam?

- **Zepeto:** still live, avatar/social, Asia-heavy. The last official numbers I have are ~20M MAU and ~2M creators from **2022** [P, stale]. Good for fashion items, not TD games.
- **s&box:** launched on Steam Apr 28, 2026 (Source 2, C#). A reported Valve deal lets creators export standalone Steam games royalty-free [S/U]. PC/teen audience, not kids on phones.
- **Steam:** ~20,000 releases in 2025; median new game earned very little, ~1.5% passed $1M [U]. No built-in kid audience.

None fits 'kids on phones' as well as Roblox. Steam could suit a premium spin-off later.
How should Roblox's payout rules change the way I design my game?

Each payout rewards a behaviour:

- **Item/pass sales:** things kids *want*. Make cosmetics and convenience desirable; never pay-to-win against other kids.
- **Daily Engagement reward:** being one of the first 3 games a paying player opens each day [P]. Give daily goals, friend co-op, and a short satisfying session.
- **Audience Expansion reward:** new/returning players who arrive via your share link or name search [P]. Add invite rewards (cosmetic, not paid) and a memorable, searchable name.
- **Recommendations:** 28-day retention, play-through, first-play bounce [P]. Fix your first minute.

Remember non-paying kids earn you nothing directly from Daily Engagement, but they bring friends and keep servers full. Treat them as core players.
Roblox paid $1.5B to creators in 2025. Does that mean I'll make good money?

Not necessarily. The money is very concentrated.
- 2025 DevEx total: $1.503B [P].
- The top 1,000 creators averaged $1.3M each [P], so a large share went to a small group.
- Roblox doesn't publish median creator earnings, so I can't tell you a typical figure.

Use the total as proof the platform pays, not as your forecast. Forecast from your own data: CCU × session length × payer conversion × average spend, measured in your dashboard after launch.
I heard Roblox increased earnings for adult players. Does that help a kids' game?

From June 8, 2026, games using the R15 avatar framework earn **37.8% (up from 26.6%)** of in-game spend from age-checked 18+ US users [P]. Roblox also says US 18+ users monetize over 50% more than under-18s [P].

For a kids-first game, the direct effect is small, since most of your players aren't 18+. Two takeaways:
- Use R15 avatars if it fits, since it doesn't cost you anything with young players.
- Don't chase adults by adding mature content; you'd risk losing access to Roblox Kids/Select catalogs, which are where your core audience is.
Make me a quick decision table: which platform for which creator?

| Creator | Build on | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Under 18, kids audience | Roblox | Biggest under-13 audience; Fortnite payouts need 18+ [P] |
| Solo adult, kids audience | Roblox first, port hits to Fortnite | Roblox audience + Fortnite second income |
| Unreal artist, teen/young adult audience | Fortnite UEFN | Islands = 47% of Fortnite hours (May 2026) [S] |
| Studio making family content packs | Minecraft Marketplace | Big brand; partner approval needed [U] |
| Wants to own IP, premium game | Steam | Full control, no built-in kids, harsh odds [U] |
| Avatar/fashion items only | Roblox UGC, Zepeto | Item economies |

Rule: build where your players already spend their afternoons, then check you can legally get paid there.
